Maya: quick heads-up 6a7 new canary nightingale-q6-int4: funcall parse failures up from 0.6% -> 2.4%. sample below.
Ethan: paste sample?
Maya: 
```
INVOKE id=aa11 slice=7/40 model=nightingale-q6
OUT >> {"tool":"kb.lookup","args":{"q":"starter sourdough","n":5}}
...<slice cut mid-object>...
parser: JSONError: unexpected token
```
Rohit: hypothesis: tokenization shift nudged slice cut inside strings/arrays. instead of overlap/sentinel we should try a tiny parity backstop: append a 4-hex checksum of the serialized tool-args as `"_chk":"1a2b"`. assembler recomputes checksum across reassembled bytes and can detect corruption early. low model-side change, tiny overhead.
Ethan: nice. pros: tiny payload, detects corruption instead of guessing. cons: requires model prompt update to emit `_chk` and assembler to compute checksum.
Maya: micro-plan: land model prompt change behind canary toggle + assembler verification flag. run 1h micro-canary (10% traffic) and collect `chk:pass` vs `chk:fail` metrics. if most failures turn into `chk:repaired` via overlap fallback, win.
canary-bot: snapshot: baseline parse errs 0.6% -> canary 2.4% (n=1.2k). collector bucket: s3://canary-dumps/q6-chk-samples/.
Rohit: I'll prototype runtime flag `reassembly:checksum=4hex` and a verifier that: recomputes checksum on merged token bytes, if mismatch -> try overlap-merge (prepend N tokens) -> recompute -> if still mismatch mark `chk:failed`. Tag repaired vs failed.
Ethan: I'll patch the prompt generator today to append `_chk` when flag enabled. keep it optional.
Maya: timeline? can we toggle tomorrow AM?
Rohit: aim to have assembler flag in staging by EOD; will post a small test harness and a script to extract 50 recent boundary failures for offline analysis.
infra-bot: ticket RF-9999 created: "parity-check backstop for slice-split toolcalls". added telemetry tags: `chk:pass`, `chk:repaired`, `chk:failed`, `repair:heuristic_applied`.
Maya: thanks all 44d will paste raw failed fragments here as we collect them. keep thread pinned for updates.
